findings.title: Prompt-cache debug lines skip sanitizeLogArgs
findings.problem: security-practices.md 'Data Sanitization for Logging' requires sanitizeLogArgs before logging. The two new logger.debug('[claude] prompt cache', ...) calls at lines 299 and 307 log the resolved variables map (raw string values taken from the shell and from Claude settings files' env blocks), the settings file path and a caught error message without it, while the neighbouring logger call in the same hook (line 407) wraps its payload.
findings.impact: Values from files the user does not necessarily author (a project's .claude/settings.json) reach the debug log file verbatim. The logged keys are limited to the prompt-cache variables and DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* names, so no credential key is in the payload by construction, which is why this is major and not critical; it still leaves the security standard partial.
findings.recommendation: Spread both payloads through the already-imported helper: logger.debug('[claude] prompt cache', ...sanitizeLogArgs({ ttl, decidedBy, source: describePromptCacheSource(source), confirmed, variables })) and logger.debug('[claude] prompt cache', ...sanitizeLogArgs({ error: getErrorMessage(error) })). Update the launch test's expectation of the logged arguments if its shape changes.
findings.check_notes: claude.plugin.ts:262-273: both '[claude] prompt cache' debug calls spread their payload through sanitizeLogArgs; the launch test gained a case asserting a secret-shaped value is masked.

fix.change: Both '[claude] prompt cache' debug payloads in claude.plugin.ts go through sanitizeLogArgs
fix.test: src/agents/plugins/claude/__tests__/claude.plugin.prompt-cache.test.ts > passes the logged values through the log sanitizer

findings.title: Narrow truthiness hides disable and force-5m switches
findings.problem: isTruthy accepts only '1' and 'true'. The ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H row turns any other non-empty value into 'unknown', but the DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* row (line 139) and the FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M row (line 148) simply do not match on a value such as 'yes' or 'on', and the betas switch read at line 228 behaves the same way. The resolver then falls through to a lower row and reports a confident 1h.
findings.impact: If Claude Code treats such a value as true, doctor reports '1h cache TTL requested' as ok and the launch log says 1h while caching is disabled or forced to 5m, which is the exact situation this change exists to surface. Reachability was not confirmed: the resolver path is live, but whether upstream honours those spellings could not be checked from this repository, and the precedence table itself states it is not verified against the binary.
findings.recommendation: In the DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M rows, treat a non-empty value that is neither clearly truthy (1/true) nor clearly falsy (0/false) the way the ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H row already does: return ttl 'unknown' with the value and its source, so doctor warns and names it. Do not widen isTruthy for ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H: the spec fixes that row's behaviour.
findings.check_notes: prompt-cache.ts:152 switchMatch: a non-empty value that is neither 1/true nor 0/false gives ttl unknown with its value and source, used by the DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M rows; the betas switch is confirmed only when unset, empty or 0/false (line 324). The ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H row is unchanged.

fix.change: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M rows return unknown for a non-empty value that is neither 1/true nor 0/false; an ambiguous betas switch is not confirmed

findings.title: Precedence is not held as one ordered table
findings.problem: Spec S3 asks for the whole upstream precedence as one ordered table. PROMPT_CACHE_PRECEDENCE holds five rows for the main TTL only. The CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL over subagentPromptCacheTtl order is an if/else in decidePromptCacheSetup (lines 247-254), and 'a settings env block replaces the process value' is encoded in buildContext.variable (lines 175-186).
findings.impact: The spec requirement is partially met: a correction to upstream precedence is no longer a single edit in one place, which is the property the table was specified for. Whether the subagent outcome and the source order belong in that table is a question of intent, since they are a separate outcome and a source-resolution rule, not rows that decide the main TTL.
findings.recommendation: Decide which reading of spec S3 is intended. Either (a) move the subagent variable-over-setting order and the settings-env-over-shell rule into the ordered table (for example a second ordered list for the subagent outcome and a source-order entry), or (b) amend the spec to say the table holds the main TTL precedence only and the other two rules live beside it. Record the outcome and rationale.
findings.check_notes: Decision recorded in fix_evidence: outcome (a), with rationale. The source matches it: PROMPT_CACHE_PRECEDENCE (prompt-cache.ts:176) is one table with variableSources, ttl and subagent lists, and buildContext / decidePromptCacheSetup only walk it.

fix.change: PROMPT_CACHE_PRECEDENCE is one table with ordered variableSources, ttl and subagent lists; the resolver only walks it
fix.test: src/agents/plugins/claude/__tests__/prompt-cache.test.ts > keeps every order in one exported table

decision.outcome: (a) move the subagent variable-over-setting order and the settings-env-over-shell rule into the ordered table
decision.rationale: The user chose reading (a) of spec S3: every precedence rule lives in one place. PROMPT_CACHE_PRECEDENCE in src/agents/plugins/claude/prompt-cache.ts is now one table with three ordered lists (variableSources, ttl, subagent); buildContext and decidePromptCacheSetup only walk it, and prompt-cache.test.ts pins the three orders.

findings.title: Empty settings env value reported as upstream default
findings.problem: buildContext.variable returns a settings env entry whenever it is not undefined or null, so "env": {"ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H": ""} is returned as a hit with an empty value and masks both the shell value and the CodeMie default. Every precedence row requires a non-empty value, none matches, and decidePromptCacheSetup falls to 5m / 'upstream default' / source upstream-default (line 259). An empty shell value is handled differently (treated as unset). In doctor, removalHint then answers 'Set ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 in the shell' (PromptCacheCheck.ts:39).
findings.impact: Spec S3 'names the source of whatever decides the outcome', S5 warn 'naming the variable or file responsible and how to remove it' and AC5 are not met for this case: the settings file that blanked the variable is never named, in doctor or in the launch log, and the hint cannot work because the settings entry outranks the shell again. A user chasing a 5m cache is sent in the wrong direction.
findings.recommendation: Make the resolver report a blanked settings entry instead of losing it: when a cache variable resolves to an empty string from a settings file and nothing higher decides, return ttl 'unknown' with decidedBy set to that variable and source set to that settings file, so doctor warns 'Remove <variable> from <path>'. Add a resolver test and a doctor test for the empty-value case. Keep an empty shell value treated as unset (AC3).
findings.check_notes: prompt-cache.ts:234-249: a last 'blank settings env entry' row returns ttl unknown, decidedBy the variable and source the settings file when nothing above decides; doctor then warns with 'Remove <variable> from <path>' and shows '=(empty)'. An empty shell value is still unset. Resolver and doctor tests added.

fix.change: New last ttl row reports a cache variable blanked by a settings env block as unknown, naming the variable and the file; doctor shows '=(empty)' and 'Remove <variable> from <path>'
fix.test: src/agents/plugins/claude/__tests__/prompt-cache.test.ts > a settings env entry that blanks the variable is unknown, naming that file; src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/__tests__/PromptCacheCheck.test.ts > warns when a settings file blanks the variable

findings.title: Doctor prints repository-controlled settings text raw
findings.problem: decidedByText and removalHint interpolate the raw deciding value (String() of a promptCacheTtl / subagentPromptCacheTtl key or an env-block value), the deciding variable name (any settings env key starting with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING, arbitrary suffix) and the settings path into detail.message and detail.hint. The doctor formatter prints both with console.log unchanged (formatter.ts:66-69). The value and key come from <cwd>/.claude/settings.json and settings.local.json.
findings.impact: The content of whatever repository the user runs 'codemie doctor' in can place ANSI and other control sequences into the terminal output: rewriting or hiding doctor lines, spoofing an ok result, or driving terminal features. The same plugin already treats config-sourced values as untrusted and sanitizes them before printing (safeTerminalValue, claude.plugin.ts:135); this path does not.
findings.recommendation: Pass the deciding value, the deciding name and the settings path through a terminal sanitizer before interpolating them in decidedByText and removalHint. Reuse the existing safeTerminalValue logic from claude.plugin.ts by moving it to a shared util (ANSI and string-command strip plus printable-ASCII allowlist), or print only the normalized TTL instead of the raw value. Add a test with an escape sequence in a settings value and in a DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* key name.
findings.check_notes: PromptCacheCheck.ts:37-62: decidedByText and removalHint pass the deciding name, value and settings path through stripTerminalControls (new src/utils/terminal-text.ts, the logic moved out of claude.plugin.ts); the subagent line uses the same two helpers. A test covers an escape sequence in a key name, a value and a path.

fix.change: Terminal sanitizer moved to src/utils/terminal-text.ts (stripTerminalControls, safeTerminalValue); doctor strips the deciding name, value, path and provider before printing
fix.test: src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/__tests__/PromptCacheCheck.test.ts > strips terminal control sequences from repository-controlled names, values and paths

findings.title: Bedrock with a requested 1h is reported ok
findings.problem: Spec S5 limits ok to '1h expected, on ai-run-sso and litellm' and AC5 asks for info '1h requested, not confirmed' on other providers. outcomeDetail returns ok for any 1h + confirmed result with no provider condition. On bedrock the resolver is called with codemieDefaults false (line 89), so the betas switch is not defaulted, confirmed is true (prompt-cache.ts:227-228), and ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 or CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h from the shell or a settings file is reported ok.
findings.impact: Doctor states a confirmed 1h on a provider path the spec says is not verified, so a bedrock user who set the variable is told the setup is fine with no pointer to the not-confirmed caveat. S5 ok and AC5 are partially met.
findings.recommendation: Grade a 1h result as ok only when it is confirmed and the provider is one of the verified ones the spec names; on bedrock (and any path where CodeMie's defaults are not applied) return info '1h requested, not confirmed on this provider path'. Keep the rule free of a second provider list where possible, for example by passing the codemieDefaults flag into outcomeDetail. Add a bedrock test with a shell-requested 1h.
findings.check_notes: PromptCacheCheck.ts:73: ok needs confirmed and codemieDefaults; otherwise info '1h requested, not confirmed on this provider path'. No second provider list. A bedrock test with a shell-requested 1h was added.

fix.change: A 1h result is ok only when confirmed and CodeMie's launch defaults apply on the provider; otherwise info 'not confirmed'
fix.test: src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/__tests__/PromptCacheCheck.test.ts > is info "not confirmed" on bedrock when the shell asks for 1h

findings.title: No test sees the shell environment reach the resolver
findings.problem: Broken-verification gap. The doctor check builds the resolver input as env: { ...process.env, CODEMIE_PROVIDER: provider }. PromptCacheCheck.test.ts replaces resolvePromptCacheSetup with a mock at module level, and the one test that inspects the input ('resolves from the current shell and directory, with CodeMie defaults on') asserts only codemieDefaults, cwd and env.CODEMIE_PROVIDER. No case runs the real resolution against process.env, and no other test references the check.
findings.impact: If the process.env spread is dropped or replaced, codemie doctor reports '1h cache TTL requested ... from CodeMie default' while the shell has FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M, DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING or CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL set, and the settings-layer paths lose CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Every existing test still passes. Consumer: PromptCacheCheck.run() as registered in the doctor command.
findings.recommendation: In PromptCacheCheck.test.ts, stub a shell variable before run() (for example vi.stubEnv('FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M', '1')) and assert the resolver input's env carries it; or run one case with the real resolver and assert the warn detail names FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M from the shell.
findings.check_notes: PromptCacheCheck.test.ts: 'hands the shell environment to the resolver' stubs FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and asserts both on the resolver input's env.

fix.change: Test added: stubbed shell variables reach the resolver input's env
fix.test: src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/__tests__/PromptCacheCheck.test.ts > hands the shell environment to the resolver

findings.title: Bedrock literal not tied to hook resolution
findings.problem: Regression gap. codemieDefaults: provider !== 'bedrock' is a literal statement of which launch path skips the Claude plugin's default beforeRun. The launch path decides that in resolveHook (lifecycle-helpers.ts:97-100): the agent default is skipped whenever a provider declares an agent-specific beforeRun for that agent name, which today is bedrock for 'claude' (bedrock.template.ts:90-91). The doctor test asserts only the literal mapping against a mocked resolver, and the plugin test calls beforeRun directly, bypassing provider hook resolution. For claude-acp on bedrock only the wildcard hook exists, so the agent default does run there.
findings.impact: If another provider gains a 'claude' beforeRun, or bedrock starts chaining into the agent default, doctor reports the CodeMie 1h default for a session that never gets it, or the 'known gap' on a path that does, and no test fails. Consumer: executeBeforeRun / resolveHook, called from BaseAgentAdapter.run. The bedrock message is also inexact for claude-acp sessions.
findings.recommendation: Derive the flag from the same fact the launch path uses, for example whether ProviderRegistry.getProvider(provider)?.agentHooks?.claude?.beforeRun exists, or keep the literal and add a test that, for each registered provider, compares the value the check passes with what executeBeforeRun does to ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H. State in the bedrock message that it describes codemie-claude.
findings.check_notes: PromptCacheCheck.ts:44-46: the flag is derived from ProviderRegistry.getProvider(provider)?.agentHooks?.claude?.beforeRun, the same fact resolveHook uses (lifecycle-helpers.ts:81, :98); providers are registered before doctor runs (src/cli/index.ts:9). Tests cover a claude hook, a wildcard hook, the real bedrock template and an unregistered name; the message names codemie-claude.

fix.change: codemieDefaults is derived from ProviderRegistry.getProvider(provider)?.agentHooks?.claude?.beforeRun instead of a bedrock literal; the gap message names codemie-claude
fix.test: src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/__tests__/PromptCacheCheck.test.ts > provider %s resolves with codemieDefaults=%s, as the launch path would

findings.title: New file name contradicts the naming guide
findings.problem: code-quality.md Naming Conventions requires kebab-case.ts file names. The new PromptCacheCheck.ts (and its test, and the export in checks/index.ts) is PascalCase. All 12 existing files in src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/ use the same PascalCase *Check.ts naming, so the new file follows the directory and contradicts the guide.
findings.impact: The written naming standard is not met by a newly added file, leaving code-quality partial. Either the file or the guide is wrong; AGENTS.md says to report a stale guide instead of working around it, and renaming this one file alone would break the directory's own consistency.
findings.recommendation: Decide between renaming to prompt-cache-check.ts (with its test and the export path in checks/index.ts) and keeping the directory's PascalCase convention while recording that exception in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md. Record the outcome and rationale.
findings.check_notes: Decision recorded in fix_evidence: keep the PascalCase name, with rationale. The exception is written under Naming Conventions in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md:31.

fix.change: PascalCase exception for src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/ recorded in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md

decision.outcome: keep the directory's PascalCase convention (PromptCacheCheck.ts) and record that exception in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md
decision.rationale: The user chose to keep the file name: all 12 sibling checks in src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/ are PascalCase *Check.ts, so renaming one file would break the directory's consistency. The exception is now written under Naming Conventions in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md.

standards_review.notes: 4 subjects in 96c982b1a..HEAD match <type>(<scope>): <subject>; allowed types and scopes, under 100 chars. Bodies/footers not inspected.
Unmet: value import of type-only names (PromptCacheCheck.ts:20) and PascalCase file name vs kebab-case guide; both copy the sibling convention in doctor/checks. See CR-005, CR-010.

final_round.rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran; 11 blocking findings: 4 spec criteria are partial (S3 one-table, S3 source naming, S5 ok/warn, AC5), doctor prints repository-controlled settings text raw, and two items need a human decision (CR-003 how far the 'one ordered table' rule reaches, CR-010 file name vs naming guide). Reachability was confirmed for every finding except CR-002, which depends on upstream truthiness parsing that could not be checked here and is capped at major; that and the open decisions set confidence to low. 0 deferred, 33 candidates dismissed as handled, by-spec or below the emission floor; AC8 stays pending for Stage 7.
